source_title: Israel polls: Netanyahu cries foul; poll chief orders probe into 'foreign hand'
source_excerpt: Israelâs election chief has ordered a probe into alleged foreign interference in the October 28 election.Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused Arab-led parties of stealing the vote and warned of a foreign takeover of parliament.The allegations emerged on Thursday as final results were awaited and neither Netanyahuâs bloc nor the opposition had secured a clear path to a majority in the 120-member Knesset.Israel's central elections committee chair, Justice Noam Sohlberg, asked Shin Bet chief David Zini to investigate suspicions of improper influence through foreign funding and alleged electoral bribery. Sohlberg said he could not confirm the validity of the claims but called for a thorough investigation. He asked Zini to submit findings within a week.Poll chief orders probe into alleged foreign interferenceSohlberg directed the Shin Bet to investigate allegations that foreign entities had sought to influence the election through funding.In his letter to Zini, he wrote, âSerious suspicions have been brought to my attention regarding improper influence on the elections â exerted through funding provided by foreign entities acting against Israeli interests.âHe added, âWhile I cannot attest to the substance of these suspicions, it is my view that â given they involve foreign entities â there is an obligation to investigate them thoroughly.âSohlberg said the Shin Bet should use its authority to establish whether evidence supported or refuted the allegations. He called the investigation necessary to protect public confidence in the electoral process and democratic institutions.The allegations have not been independently established. Sohlberg did not identify the countries allegedly involved or provide further details about the suspected interference.Netanyahu accuses Arab parties of stealing electionsNetanyahu seized on the investigation to intensify his attack on Arab-led parties and oppose any attempt by his rivals to form a government with their support.In a post on X, he said, âThe Ra'amgate affair is an earthquake. They stole the elections in Israel!âHe added: âThis is an attack on democracy whose purpose is to lead to a foreign takeover of the Knesset, the Islamization of Israel, and the overthrow of right-wing rule in order to lead to retreat and defeat of the IDF in all arenas - and primarily Iran.âNetanyahu also called for immediate action by the security agency and police. âWe demand to act immediately and with all means available to the Shin Bet and the police to investigate these crimes,â he said.Likud has argued that the allegations should rule out cooperation between Zionist parties and the Arab-led Raâam and Joint List parties. It warned against forming a government with their support or replacing the Knesset speaker through what it described as votes bought with cash.The accusations remain claims made by Netanyahu and his party. Police have previously said there was âno supporting evidenceâ for Likudâs allegation that Arab-led parties stole the election.Likud suspects Qatar and Turkey behind alleged fundingNetanyahuâs Likud party suspects Qatar and Turkey may have funded get-out-the-vote groups targeting Arab citizens in Israel, according to Hebrew-language media reports.Channel 12 reported that the investigation was based on intelligence received by the Shin Bet and presented to Sohlberg. The reports said the channels allegedly used to transfer money to the organisations closely resembled those previously used to send funds for terrorism.However, the alleged involvement of Qatar and Turkey has not been established. Sohlberg did not identify any country as being behind the suspected interference.The allegations have taken on greater political significance because Arab-led parties could help Netanyahuâs opponents secure a majority. The investigation could therefore influence the debate over whether opposition parties should cooperate with them to form a government.Four arrested in alleged voter bribery caseFour men were arrested on Thursday and were being questioned by the Lahav 433 major crimes unit over an alleged voter bribery scheme, Israeli police said.The arrests followed the detention of three southern Bedouin men on election day, Tuesday, on suspicion of planning to pay people to vote for Raâam.Raâam has identified the men as party activists and denied the allegations. It remains unclear whether the arrests are connected to the Shin Betâs investigation into suspected foreign interference.The separate bribery case has added to the political controversy surrounding the election. However, the arrests do not by themselves establish that the alleged scheme took place or that foreign actors were involved.Neither Netanyahu nor opposition has a clear majorityThe election has left Israel facing a difficult coalition-building process. Local media projections put Netanyahuâs bloc at 53 seats, opposition parties at 48 and Arab-led parties at 19 in the 120-member Knesset.A party or bloc needs at least 61 seats to secure a parliamentary majority. Neither Netanyahuâs allies nor the opposition can currently reach that threshold on their own.The Arab-led parties could therefore play a decisive role in determining the next government, even if they do not join a formal coalition.Netanyahuâs Likud party has received the most votes, but that does not automatically guarantee him another term. The president traditionally asks the leader of the party with the most votes to try to form a government, although this is not a legal requirement.Eisenkot open to cooperation with Arab-led partiesNetanyahuâs chief rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, has said he is open to working with Arab-led parties to reach the 61-seat threshold.Ahmad Tibi, head of the Joint List, told Army Radio that the opposition bloc had approached him about replacing the Knesset speaker. He said his party would support the blocâs candidate and urged Eisenkot to show political courage.The Joint List described the election result as an âunprecedented show of strengthâ by Arab voters and praised Jewish voters âwilling to swim against the tide of racism.âSmall rallies were held overnight in Tel Aviv and Jerusalem in support of a coalition that includes Arab-led parties.Such cooperation would be politically significant. Until 2021, no Arab party had joined an Israeli coalition government. The brief participation of an Arab party in a coalition that year marked a historic departure.Netanyahuâs party is seeking to use the foreign interference allegations to discourage such an arrangement. The opposition, meanwhile, faces the challenge of building a majority without abandoning its central campaign pledge to remove him from power.Final results expected after absentee ballots are countedFinal election results could come as early as Thursday evening, once around half a million absentee ballots have been counted. The ballots include votes from military personnel, diplomats, prisoners, hospital patients and others.The votes are not expected to alter the overall result dramatically, according to the available projections.Israelâs election results must be certified by November 4. President Isaac Herzog is expected to task someone with forming the next government the following week.The swearing-in of the new parliament is scheduled for November 10. Eisenkot has warned political actors against using the investigation to influence the timing of the process.If coalition negotiations fail after multiple attempts, Israel could face another election early next year. Herzog has indicated that he wants to avoid that outcome.Political deadlock comes amid deep divisionsThe election has exposed divisions over security, religion and the future direction of Israel.One major issue is whether the fast-growing ultra-Orthodox population should continue to be exempt from compulsory military service. The question has become more contentious after three years of inconclusive wars and military losses.Netanyahu, Israelâs longest-serving prime minister, remains a polarising figure. The Trump administration has spoken of new attacks after the US midterm elections on November 3.Experts have suggested that Netanyahu could use a renewed, large-scale conflict to push for a national unity government under his leadership.Such a development could also delay calls for a public inquiry into the security failures surrounding the Hamas-led attack on October 7, 2023, the deadliest extremist attack in Israelâs history, which triggered the war in Gaza.For now, the election investigation, the unresolved parliamentary arithmetic and the dispute over cooperation with Arab-led parties are likely to shape the next phase of government formation.
